svg.title: A tangent line approximation and why it overestimates
svg.desc: The graph of y = square root of x (crimson) for x from 0 to 9.5 and its tangent line at (4, 2), L(x) = 2 + (x minus 4)/4 (blue). At x = 7 the line gives L(7) = 2.75 while the square root of 7 is about 2.646. A zoomed panel near x = 7 shows the line above the curve. Because the graph is concave down, the tangent line lies above it and the approximation is an overestimate.
